title: Tiny packets
summary: The buckets are ordinary programs. The fabric carries the “I tipped” notes.

cards.text:
Each tip is a tiny packet: who tipped.
When it arrives is the when.

The neuron model is software, so you can change it.
The cost is energy. This is not the thriftiest chip.

choices: The fabric that moves huge numbers of tiny packets
question.why: The cores are deliberately ordinary ARM cores.
question.simpler: The 2014 paper had thousands of processors, and a million-core machine as the aim.

question.prompt: An unusual neuron written in software is a natural fit here.
question.why: You change the model by changing code.
question.simpler: A fixed on-chip learning microcode is the other chip’s bet.

recall.question: On SpiNNaker, is the neuron model fixed silicon or software?

deeper.note: Furber, Galluppi, Temple, and Plana. Read the packet and the programming model. Do not promote the aim into a finished million-core result.

paper.title: The SpiNNaker Project
paper.section: The packet and the real-time programming model.

terms.plain: a spike as a tiny message
terms.definition: A packet that says which neuron fired. Arrival time is the timestamp.
